_comment: Adversarial benchmark. Fully synthetic — no real patients, no real clinicians. Each case has a transcript (ground truth conversation), a note_under_test (what an ambient scribe supposedly produced), and ground_truth describing any deliberately injected error. Expanded from a 6-case starter set to 18, and from 18 to the current 60: 10 numeric_medication_error, 10 fabrication, 10 negation_error, 8 distortion, 7 misattribution, 7 omission, 8 clean controls (no planted error, used to measure false-positive rate). Note that the results reported in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md cover 57 of these 60 - three cases errored out mid-run and are excluded there rather than counted as misses; see that file's 'Current auto-scored results' section. The omission category was added once the pipeline actually gained a way to detect it (see src/pipeline.py's omission_check_batch) — before that, planting omission cases would have scored 0% against a detector that didn't exist.

Plan: Nitrofurantoin 100mg twice daily for 5 days. Increase fluid intake. Return precautions given for fever or back pain.

Doctor: Any numbness in the foot?
Patient: No.

Objective: Swelling and tenderness over the lateral malleolus. No posterior malleolar bony tenderness. Able to bear weight; Ottawa ankle rules not met, imaging not indicated.
Assessment: Lateral ankle sprain.
Plan: Ice, compression, elevation, ibuprofen as needed. Begin gentle range of motion in several days. Return to sport in 2-3 weeks once pain-free.

Doctor: Tell me about the eye.
Patient: The right eye's been red and watery for two days. There's some crusting in the morning.
Doctor: Any pain, or change in your vision?
Patient: No pain, and I can see fine.
Doctor: Do you wear contact lenses?
Patient: No, just glasses.
Doctor: Anyone at home or work with the same thing?
Patient: My son had a red eye last week.
Doctor: This looks like a viral conjunctivitis. It should clear on its own in a week or so.
Patient: Do I need drops?
Doctor: No antibiotics needed. Cool compresses, wash your hands often, and don't share towels. Come back if you get pain or your vision changes.
cases.note_under_test:
Subjective: Patient reports two days of right eye redness and tearing with morning crusting. Denies eye pain or visual change. Does not wear contact lenses. Sick contact: son with red eye last week.
Objective: Right conjunctival injection without corneal involvement. Vision grossly intact.
Assessment: Viral conjunctivitis.
Plan: Supportive care with cool compresses. Hand hygiene, avoid sharing towels. No antibiotics indicated. Return precautions for eye pain or vision change.
